newsitem.title: USA: CME June hogs move higher on strong pork prices.
newsitem.headline: CME June hogs move higher on strong pork prices.

text.p: CME June hog futures moved sharply higher in early trading in reaction to higher cash pork prices Wednesday, particularly loins, and to talk cash prices will be higher Thursday, traders said.
Rand Financial and Refco were featured buying the June hogs and Rand also bought July. June extended gains when buy-stops were hit near 83.95 cents per lb.
USDA reported pork cutout values rose $0.42 to $0.46 per hundredweight, but 14- to 22-lb loins were up $2.00 at $139.00, a $5.00 gain from the $134.00 quote a week ago.
Traders were unable to give a reason for the rise in loin prices, but said the gains should help lift cash hog prices.
At 1035 CDT, CME hog futures were up 1.175 to 0.250 cents with June up the most at 84.725 cents per lb.
